name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
variant: Supinated dumbbell curl performed seated on an incline bench with the shoulders extended behind the torso; standing, preacher, cable, and machine curls are separate variants.
description: Set an incline bench low enough that the arms hang slightly behind the torso, sit back with the shoulders quiet, curl the dumbbells without letting the elbows drift forward, then lower under control until the elbows are long and the biceps are loaded at the bottom.

hypertrophy.rationale: Strong biceps accessory with a useful lengthened bottom position, but still a narrow single-joint movement.

strength.rationale: The incline position is useful for local elbow-flexor strength, but it limits absolute loading compared with standing or bar variants.

joint_resilience.rationale: The lengthened shoulder position can build tolerance if loaded modestly, but it is not broadly resilient and can be uncomfortable if overdone.

athletic_transfer.rationale: Transfer is very narrow because the movement isolates elbow flexion on a bench.

control.rationale: Requires control of shoulder drift, wrist position, and lower-end range, but little balance or bracing.

fatigue_efficiency.rationale: Focused local stimulus with low systemic fatigue, though the lengthened position can create more local soreness than easier curl variants.

setup.rationale: Requires an adjustable bench and matching dumbbells, with bench angle affecting repeatability.

ease.rationale: Simple once positioned, but shoulder extension and bottom range need more care than a standing curl.

progression.rationale: Load and reps are easy to record, but dumbbell jumps and bench angle changes can blur comparisons.

support.rationale: The bench supports the torso, but the shoulders, elbows, and wrists remain free.

primary.name: Biceps brachii
primary.evidenceShort: Incline dumbbell curl EMG directly measures biceps brachii.
primary.evidence: Incline dumbbell curl EMG directly measured biceps brachii activity and compared it with standing and preacher positions. Shoulder-extended curl training evidence also supports biceps brachii adaptation in lengthened-position curl patterns.

secondary.name: Brachialis
secondary.evidenceShort: Deep elbow flexor contribution is expected during loaded elbow flexion.
secondary.evidence: Brachialis is included from elbow-flexor anatomy and supported by shoulder-position curl training evidence assessing brachialis thickness. It is secondary because the strongest direct incline EMG evidence is for biceps brachii.

secondary.name: Brachioradialis
secondary.evidenceShort: Curl EMG studies directly measure brachioradialis contribution.
secondary.evidence: Dumbbell and handgrip curl EMG measured brachioradialis activity. It is secondary because a supinated incline curl remains primarily a biceps brachii movement.

support.name: Wrist flexors
support.evidenceShort: Grip and wrist posture require forearm support.
support.evidence: Forearm EMG evidence supports wrist flexor involvement in grip and wrist-position control. The role is support only because the primary task is elbow flexion.

evidence.verdict: Incline dumbbell curl: biceps brachii primary; brachialis and brachioradialis secondary; wrist flexors support.
evidence.clinicalShort: Shoulder-extended curls alter biceps loading; EMG and thickness studies do not remove the need to track bench angle and range.
evidence.limitsShort: Bench angle, shoulder extension, elbow drift, bottom range, supination, load, and tempo can materially change the stimulus.
evidence.summary: The incline dumbbell curl is classified as a shoulder-extended dumbbell elbow-flexion accessory. Direct incline curl EMG supports biceps brachii as the primary visible target. Brachialis and brachioradialis are included as secondary elbow-flexor contributors from curl training and EMG evidence, while wrist flexors are support for grip and wrist control.
evidence.clinicalInterpretation: This variant should be tracked separately from standing and preacher curls because the shoulder-extended starting position changes length, comfort, loading tolerance, and likely adaptation profile.
evidence.limitations: Bench angle and shoulder position are central to the exercise. If a user sits too upright, lets the elbows drift forward, or shortens the lower range, the movement becomes closer to a seated dumbbell curl than an incline dumbbell curl.

studies.finding: Compared biceps brachii EMG across incline dumbbell curl, standing dumbbell curl, and preacher curl conditions.
studies.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MAC, Vieira TMM. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. Journal of Sports Science and Medicine. 2009;8(1):24-29.
studies.relevance: Direct incline dumbbell curl evidence for biceps brachii activity.

studies.shortCitation: Attarieh et al., Eur J Sport Sci, 2025
studies.finding: Compared shoulder-flexed preacher curl and shoulder-extended Bayesian cable curl training for biceps brachii and brachialis thickness and strength outcomes.
studies.citation: Attarieh M, Jo E, Ribeiro AS, et al. Comparison Between Shoulder Flexed and Extended Positions During Cable Biceps Curls for Biceps Brachii and Brachialis Muscle Growth and Elbow Flexor Strength. European Journal of Sport Science. 2025.
studies.relevance: Close shoulder-extended curl evidence for biceps and brachialis adaptation boundaries.

studies.finding: Straight barbell, EZ-bar, and dumbbell curls produced different biceps brachii and brachioradialis EMG patterns across repetition phases.
studies.citation: Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, Moro T, Grigoletto D, Piccolo D, Paoli A. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ. 2018;6:e5165. doi:10.7717/peerj.5165.
studies.relevance: Dumbbell curl evidence for brachioradialis contribution and curl-family boundaries.

studies.finding: Supinated, pronated, and neutral cable curl handgrips changed biceps brachii, brachioradialis, and anterior deltoid excitation in competitive bodybuilders.
studies.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Toninelli N, Padovan R, Esposito F, Ce E. Biceps Brachii and Brachioradialis Excitation in Biceps Curl Exercise: Different Handgrips, Different Synergy. Sports. 2023;11(3):64. doi:10.3390/sports11030064.
studies.relevance: Handgrip-specific curl evidence for brachioradialis contribution and grip boundaries.

studies.type: Forearm rotation and wrist muscle EMG
studies.shortCitation: Ikeda et al., J Orthop Surg Res, 2025
studies.finding: Wrist flexor and extensor activity changed with forearm rotation during controlled wrist torque tasks.
studies.citation: Ikeda K, Kaneoka K, Matsunaga N, Ikumi A, Yamazaki M, Yoshii Y. Effects of forearm rotation on wrist flexor and extensor muscle activities. Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research. 2025;20(1):53. doi:10.1186/s13018-024-05363-x.
studies.relevance: Forearm and wrist-position evidence for grip and wrist support.

studies.type: Forearm EMG during wrist and finger movements
studies.finding: Multi-channel EMG quantified forearm muscle activity during wrist and finger movement tasks.
studies.citation: Gazzoni M, Celadon N, Mastrapasqua D, Paleari M, Margaria V, Ariano P. Quantifying forearm muscle activity during wrist and finger movements by means of multi-channel electromyography. PLoS ONE. 2014;9(10):e109943. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0109943.
studies.relevance: Broader forearm EMG context for gripping and wrist-position stabilization.
